summary: Pitts Town Airport (PWN/MYCP) is a small public airfield serving Pitts Town on Crooked Island, part of the remote Acklins and Crooked Island District in the southern Bahamas. It provides essential air access to a sparsely populated island chain known for its unspoiled beaches, historic Loyalist-era settlements, and excellent bonefishing. The modest single-runway facility primarily handles light aircraft and inter-island commuter flights.
faqs:
Q: What is Pitts Town Airport primarily used for?
A: The airport mainly serves inter-island domestic flights, private general aviation, and small charter aircraft connecting Crooked Island to Nassau and other Bahamian islands.

Q: Which airlines fly into Pitts Town Airport?
A: Small regional and charter operators, including Bahamasair-affiliated services and private charters, serve the airport on a limited schedule.

Q: Is there a terminal building at PWN?
A: The airport has minimal infrastructure typical of small Bahamian airfields, with basic facilities and no large commercial terminal.

Q: Are there customs and immigration services at Pitts Town Airport?
A: Customs services are limited or unavailable; international travelers typically clear immigration at Nassau before connecting to the island.
transport_tips: Ground transportation options are minimal, so arrange a rental vehicle or pickup with a local guesthouse or hotel in advance. Taxis may be available but are not guaranteed without prior booking. The nearest settlement of Pitts Town is only a short drive from the airport terminal.
local_tip: Stock up on supplies and fuel in Nassau or another major hub before flying in, as Crooked Island has very limited services, shops, and fuel availability outside the main settlements.
